title: variable-window cohort packer: lookahead cohorting for seqlen-aware continuous batching
author: Ava M. Chen
release_notes: Introduce a variable-time-window cohort packing heuristic that groups incoming requests into short-lived cohorts based on observed sequence-length distribution and a small lookahead buffer; reduces padding and improves kernel alignment for mixed-length workloads. Backwards-compatible toggle via runtime flag and rollout config.
description:
Context and motivation: Mixed-length traffic in customer workloads causes large padding inefficiencies when using fixed bucketing or single-window continuous batching. Prior PRs implemented static bucketing and slot-duration batching, but we still see suboptimal kernel utilization when short and long sequences interleave. This PR introduces a variable-window cohort packing heuristic that forms transient cohorts using a small lookahead window and a seqlen-aware cost model. Motivation: reduce padding tokens across the common long-tail of sequence lengths, improve kernel alignment (so kernels process similarly shaped tensors), and maintain SLOs for p50/p95/p99 latency.

Design summary: Implemented a cohort_packer that buffers incoming requests for a variable delta (configurable: default 8ms max lookahead) and groups them into cohorts by a lightweight seqlen cost heuristic. The heuristic computes an expected padding cost and a kernel-alignment benefit score; cohorts are closed when marginal cost of adding a request exceeds a threshold or when the lookahead timer fires. A smoothing factor prevents starving long requests: if a request exceeds a seqlen threshold it gets a higher urgency weight, which reduces its maximum wait time. The packer integrates with the existing continuous batcher by emitting micro-batches aligned to kernel-friendly shapes.

Runtime and kernel changes: Added kernel selection hints from cohort metadata so the kernel_selector can prefer fused kernels (e.g., grouped attention fast path) when cohort variance is low. Added a small KV cache warm-start hint that tags cohorts containing continuation requests; runtime can prefetch KV segments for those cohorts to avoid cold-cache spikes. The scheduler slot_prioritizer receives cohort urgency scores to decide slot assignment order to avoid head-of-line blocking.

Files and high-level diffs: Summaries of the nine modified files: cohort_packer.cpp/.h (new core heuristic, config parsing, tests hooks), slot_prioritizer.cpp (uses cohort urgency to prioritize), kernel_selector.cpp (adds hint processing and a small selection rule), kv_warm_hint.cpp (attach warm-start metadata to cohorts), microbench harness and example runner, rollout config, and a short doc explaining the runtime flag. No public API changes.

Commits (high-level):
- feat(cohort): initial variable-window cohort packer implementation and tests
- perf(batcher): integrate cohort packer with continuous batcher and add kernel hints
- feat(kv): kv warm-start hint plumbing and unit tests
- perf(scheduler): integrate cohort urgency into slot prioritizer
- test(bench): microbench for mixed seqlen workload and CI benchmark job
- docs: rollout guide and tuning notes

Performance experiments: Benchmarked on p4d-like cluster using mixed synthetic workload (short=8–16 tokens, medium=64–128, long=512–1024) and a production-sampled trace. Results on our perf cluster: median padding tokens per batch reduced by ~22% on synthetic mix and ~18% on production trace; token cost reduced 8–12% depending on model; overall throughput increased 6–9% for mixed workloads. P99 latency improved up to 15% in congestion scenarios due to urgency weighting and reduced head-of-line blocking. KV-warm hints reduced KV miss spikes for continuation-heavy cohorts by ~30%.

Testing and CI: Added unit tests for the cohort closure logic, fuzz tests for edge windows, and an end-to-end microbenchmark that runs in CI (marked flaky on first run and rerun automatically). CI initially reported a flaky benchmark timeout; retriggering the job passed and the PR shows final CI status as pass.

Rollout plan: Feature gated by runtime flag `enable_variable_cohorting` and rollout config in configs/rollouts. Canary rollout to 5% of serving nodes for three days, then 25% if error and latency budgets hold, then 100%. Observability: added cohort-level metrics (cohort_size, avg_padding, avg_wait_ms, kv_warm_hits) and tracing tags for cohort_id to help perf debugging.

Review notes and discussion (summary):
- Reviewer Miguel: requested clarification on starvation bounds and suggested explicit max-wait enforcement for long sequences; addressed by urgency weight and added tests.
- Reviewer Priya: asked for more telemetry; added cohort-level metrics and a small dashboard query in docs.
- Reviewer Liam: requested kernel selection API to remain advisory (non-blocking); adjusted kernel_selector to treat cohort hints as soft preferences.
- Post-approval: small follow-up perf tweak to default lookahead from 12ms to 8ms after canary showed slight latency bump on very bursty workloads.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc inline (docs/running/variable_cohorting.md)
- [x] Unit tests and microbench
- [x] CI green (after rerun)
- [x] Rollout config and metrics
- [x] No public API breaking changes

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main on 2026-02-25 after approvals.

Notes for follow-ups: Evaluate interplay with existing seqlen bucketing when both are enabled (there is a small compatibility note in docs), and consider exposing an adaptive lookahead controller in a later PR that tunes the window based on observed arrival variance.
examples: See examples/benchmarks/ci_mixed_seqlen_runner.py for workload driver used in experiments
additional_notes: This PR was mostly code in the runtime path; perf-team validated with independent harness and RKD trace slice. No infra changes required for rollout.
